chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the woman whose husband dies while she is in her waiting period (Iddah), can she go out for a right (claim/affair)? He said: Indeed, some of the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) asked him, saying: 'So-and-so woman's husband died, so she wants to go out for a right that is due to her.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'Uff to you! Before I was sent, when a woman from you had her husband die, she would take a clod of cow dung and throw it behind her back.'

Then she said: 'I shall neither comb my hair, nor apply kohl, nor dye (henna) for a full year. But I have only commanded you with four months and ten days. Then, be patient (in abstaining): do not comb, do not apply kohl, do not dye, do not go out from her house during the day, and do not spend the night away from her house.'

She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what should she do if a right presents itself to her?' He said: 'She goes out after the decline of the night (midnight), and returns at evening, so she is considered not to have spent the night away from her house.'
I said to him: 'Can she perform Hajj?' He said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a widow going out during her Iddah period in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the balance between mourning restrictions and practical necessity for a widow in her Iddah, distinguishing between the pre-Islamic custom of extended seclusion and the Prophetic limit of four months and ten days. It establishes that leaving the home for legal rights (Haqq) is permissible provided she returns before nightfall, thereby preserving the core requirement of not spending the night away from her residence. The narration further confirms that this allowance extends to performing Hajj, demonstrating the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in accommodating essential religious duties during the waiting period.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the woman widowed from her husband, and she happens to be in her waiting period, can she go out regarding a right?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘One of the wives of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> asked him<sup>saww</sup> saying, ‘So and so woman has been widowed from her husband, so she wants to go out regarding a right on his behalf’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to her: ‘Uff! You (women), before I<sup>saww</sup> was Sent, whenever a woman from you was widowed from her husband, would take cow dung and, so she would throw it behind her back.

Then she said, ‘I shall neither comb (hair), nor apply Kohl, nor dye, for a whole year. But rather, I<sup>saww</sup> have ordered you all (women) with four months and ten (days), then she is not being patient from not combing, nor applying Kohl, nor dye, nor going out from her house during the day, nor spending a night away from her house?’

So she said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! So how should she act if a right presented itself to her?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘She can go out after the decline of the night (midnight), and return during the evening, thus she would become not having spent a night away from her house’.
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can she perform Hajj?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a woman whose husband dies; if it is proper for her to perform al-Hajj and visit the sick people. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, she can do so for the sake of Allah, but must not use kohl and perfume.’”
